title: Molecular Dynamics Study on Wear Resistance of High Entropy Alloy Coatings Considering the Effect of Temperature

recollection.starting_material: High entropy alloy (likely equiatomic or near-equiatomic multicomponent metallic system, e.g., CoCrFeNi or derivatives) model slabs in an atomistic simulation cell
recollection.intervention: Classical molecular-dynamics sliding wear simulations; varied the ambient temperature across several values (e.g., 300 K–1000 K) while dragging a diamond or rigid indenter tip across the HEA surface
recollection.structure: Generated an amorphized or nanocrystalline tribolayer on the HEA surface whose thickness and defect density depended on temperature
recollection.mechanism: Wear resistance determined by competition between dislocation-mediated plasticity and thermally activated atomic diffusion; higher temperature promoted atomic mixing and decreased stacking-fault energy, facilitating material removal
recollection.results: Predicted that the wear rate (atoms removed per sliding length) increased roughly two- to three-fold when temperature rose from room temperature to 800–1000 K; identified a critical temperature above which wear accelerates sharply; hardness and friction coefficient dropped by ~20–30 % at the highest temperature; alloying-element local segregation near the surface contributed to self-lubricating behavior at moderate temperatures

score.note: The recollection generically identifies temperature-varied MD wear/indenter simulations, but misses the specific nanoindentation protocol, temperatures, depth, and speeds. The proposed tribolayer, diffusion/segregation mechanism, wear-rate increase, and friction decrease are unsupported or conflict with the paper. It also omits the reported hardness and modulus values and substantially misstates their changes.
